plants.name: Wisteria floribunda
plants.description: Cascading chains of fragrant, pea-like flowers drip from ancient twining vines, forming glowing violet curtains over temple trellises and garden pergolas. Bees hum through the blossoms as the scent drifts on the spring air.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-April to early May in Kyoto, with blooms peaking in late April
plants.location: Kyoto, Japan (e.g. Byodo-in Temple in Uji)
plants.funFact: Wisteria vines twine in a set direction. Japanese wisteria climbs clockwise, while Chinese wisteria climbs counterclockwise. Some vines live for well over a century and can crush sturdy supports as they grow.

plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: Cup-shaped blooms in nearly every colour imaginable stand in ruler-straight rows across flat Dutch farmland. From above, the fields look like a vast striped patchwork quilt.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-April to early May in the Netherlands, with Keukenhof's display running through spring
plants.location: Lisse and the Bollenstreek bulb region, the Netherlands
plants.funFact: In the 1630s, tulip bulbs became so sought after in the Dutch Republic that single bulbs reportedly sold for more than the price of a canal house. This episode is remembered as one of history's first speculative bubbles.

plants.name: Cercis canadensis
plants.description: Before a single leaf unfurls, bare branches and even trunks erupt in clusters of tiny magenta-pink, pea-like flowers. Woodland edges across eastern North America glow with pink haze. Heart-shaped leaves follow once the blooms fade.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to mid spring, typically April, lasting two to three weeks
plants.location: Eastern and central United States, from woodland edges to home gardens
plants.funFact: Redbud is one of the few trees that practices cauliflory, producing flowers directly from old branches and trunks. The young blossoms are edible, with a mildly tangy flavour that works in salads.
